topic.title: Integrating Web Author with a File Storage Service

keywords.indexterm: Integration with a file storage service

body.p: If you want content contributors to be able to open and save files in , you must first integrate it with your file storage system. The complexity of the integration depends on the file storage service you use.

section.title: Integration via Configuration
section.p: You can integrate with Git, GitHub, SharePoint, or a generic CMIS connector by changing the server configuration. The same applies to any CMS that supports WebDAV. A system administrator can configure these integrations in the web-based Administration Page.

section.title: Integration via REST API
section.p: With this approach, you extend your file storage service to expose a simple REST API that can be processed by . To use this approach, you need software development skills and access to the API documentation of the file storage service. It is the best choice for CMS developers and for companies with in-house file storage systems.

section.title: Integration via a Custom Plugin
section.p: If you are developing a CMS or have complex integration requirements, consider using the low-level Java API to implement the integration. Start with the REST API for the first version of the integration. If it does not meet your requirements, use a custom plugin.
One of the biggest challenges of implementing support for a file storage system is user authentication. For information about CMS authentication, see and .
To see the detailed steps required to implement a connector from scratch, see the Integrate Web Author with a File Storage Service with a Custom Plugin topic.
This is the approach used to implement the connector for WebDAV and for the REST API. The source code for these connectors is available on GitHub and can serve as a reference.
